indicativo.title: Indicativo
indicativo.summary: The mood of facts: what happens, happened or will happen.
body: The indicative presents something as real or certain. Unless something calls for another mood, the verb is in the indicative.

head: Tense
Example
Expresses
rows: Now, habits, general truths, the near future
Past habits, descriptions, actions in progress
Past actions linked to the present
Completed actions in a finished time
Just before another past action, literary
The future, guesses about the present
Before a future moment, guesses about the past

body: Every compound tense is *haber* in the matching simple tense, plus the participle, which never changes.
Statements of knowledge take the indicative: *Sé que {ip:habla} bien.* Wishes, doubts and denied opinions take the subjunctive: *Quiero que {csp:hable}. No creo que {csp:hable} bien.*

presente.title: Presente
presente.summary: What is happening now, what usually happens, and often the near future.
body: Remove *-ar*, *-er* or *-ir* and add the endings.
The stressed vowel changes everywhere except in *nosotros* and *vosotros*.
Irregular only in *yo*: *hacer: hago; poner: pongo; salir: salgo; traer: traigo; conocer: conozco; saber: sé; dar: doy; ver: veo.* *Venir* and *decir* have *vengo, vienes* and *digo, dices*.

ul: Something happening now: *{ip:Leo} el periódico.* To stress that it is in progress, use *estar* with the gerund: *{ip:Estoy} leyendo.*
Habits: *Los lunes {ip:voy} al gimnasio.*
General truths: *El agua {ip:hierve} a cien grados.*
The near future: *Mañana {ip:salgo} para Madrid.*
An action that still continues: *{ip:Estudio} español desde hace dos años.*

imperfecto.title: Imperfecto
imperfecto.summary: The past seen from the inside: habits, descriptions and actions in progress.
body: *-ar* verbs take *-aba*. *-er* and *-ir* verbs share *-ía*.

ul: Past habits: *De niño {im:iba} a la playa cada verano.*
Descriptions of people, places, weather and states: *{im:Era} tarde y {im:llovía}.*
An action in progress when something else happened: *{im:Dormía} cuando {pr:llegó} Marcos.*
Polite requests: *{im:Quería} un café, por favor.*

body: The *imperfecto* gives the background or a state with no clear end. The *indefinido* tells what happened: *{im:Hacía} frío, así que {pr:cerré} la ventana.*

preterito_perfecto.title: Pretérito perfecto
preterito_perfecto.summary: A past action still connected to the present.
body: Use the present of *haber* and the participle: *-ar* becomes *-ado*, *-er* and *-ir* become *-ido*. The auxiliary is always *haber* and the participle never changes.
Nothing can come between the two parts. Pronouns go first: *Me {pp:he levantado} tarde.*

ul: A time period that is not over: *Hoy {pp:he comido} tarde. Esta semana {pp:he trabajado} mucho.*
Life experience: *¿{pp:Has estado} en México?*
Recent events that still matter: *{pp:He perdido} las llaves.*
In much of Latin America the *indefinido* is preferred in these contexts: *Hoy comí tarde.*

pluscuamperfecto.title: Pluscuamperfecto
body: Use the *imperfecto* of *haber* and the participle.

ul: An action completed before another past event: *Cuando {pr:llegué}, el tren ya {tp:había salido}.*
The cause of a past situation: *{im:Estaba} cansado porque {tp:había trabajado} todo el día.*
Reported speech: *Dijo que {tp:había terminado}.*
First-time experiences: *Nunca {tp:había visto} algo así.*

indefinido.title: Indefinido
indefinido.summary: Completed actions in a finished period of time. Also called pretérito perfecto simple.
body: *-er* and *-ir* verbs share the same endings. The written accent matters: *hablo* is I speak, *habló* is he spoke.
Spelling in *yo*: *buscar: busqué; llegar: llegué; empezar: empecé.*
*-ir* stem-changing verbs change in the third person: *pedir: pidió, pidieron; dormir: durmió, durmieron.*
Many verbs have a special stem and unstressed endings, with no written accent.
Also: *estar: estuve; poder: pude; poner: puse; saber: supe; querer: quise; venir: vine; dar: di; ver: vi.*

ul: Actions in a finished time, with words like *ayer* or *el año pasado*: *Ayer {pr:fui} al cine.*
A sequence of events: *{pr:Me levanté}, {pr:desayuné} y {pr:salí}.*
An event that interrupts: *{im:Dormía} cuando {pr:sonó} el teléfono.*
Dates and history: *Cervantes {pr:murió} en 1616.*

preterito_anterior.title: Pretérito anterior
preterito_anterior.summary: A rare literary tense: one action immediately before another.
body: Use the *indefinido* of *haber* and the participle.
It appears after *apenas, en cuanto, tan pronto como, cuando* and *después de que*, with the main verb in the *indefinido*: *Apenas {tr:hubo terminado}, {pr:salió}.*
You only need to recognise it. Today people say *Apenas {pr:terminó}, {pr:salió}* or use the *pluscuamperfecto*.

futuro_simple.title: Futuro simple
futuro_simple.summary: What will happen, and guesses about the present.
body: Add the endings to the whole infinitive. All three verb groups share them.

ul: Future events and predictions: *El año que viene {fs:iremos} a Japón.*
Promises: *Te lo {fs:devolveré}.*
A guess about the present: *¿Qué hora es? {fs:Serán} las ocho.*
For plans, speakers often prefer *ir a* with the infinitive: *{ip:Voy} a estudiar.*

body: After *cuando* and similar words a future event takes the subjunctive: *Cuando {csp:llegues}, te {fs:llamaré}.* After *si* it takes the present: *Si {ip:llueve}, me {fs:quedaré} en casa.*

futuro_compuesto.title: Futuro compuesto
futuro_compuesto.summary: What will already have happened, and guesses about the past.
body: Use the *futuro simple* of *haber* and the participle.

ul: An action finished by a future moment: *Para las diez {fa:habré terminado}.*
A guess about the recent past: *No ha llegado: {fa:habrá perdido} el tren.*

condicional.title: Condicional
condicional.summary: What would happen: politeness, advice, wishes and hypotheses.
body: It presents an action as dependent on a condition or softens what is said. Modern Spanish grammar counts it as a tense of the indicative, but it behaves very much like its own mood.

head: Form
Example
Refers to
rows: Now, the future, the future seen from the past

body: The *si* clause takes the subjunctive, and the conditional goes in the result clause.

ul: Possible now: *Si {csi:tuviera} tiempo, {cop:viajaría}.*
Impossible, in the past: *Si {cst:hubiera tenido} tiempo, {cpa:habría viajado}.*
Past condition, present result: *Si {cst:hubiera estudiado}, ahora {cop:sabría} la respuesta.*

condicional_simple.title: Condicional simple
condicional_simple.summary: Would do: polite requests, advice, wishes, hypotheses.
body: Add *-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían* to the whole infinitive.
They are the same as in the future: {cop:tendría}, {cop:pondría}, {cop:saldría}, {cop:vendría}, {cop:podría}, {cop:sabría}, {cop:habría}, {cop:querría}, {cop:diría}, {cop:haría}.

ul: Polite requests: *¿{cop:Podría} ayudarme?*
Advice: *{cop:Deberías} dormir más.*
Wishes: *Me {cop:gustaría} vivir junto al mar.*
The result of a hypothesis: *Si {csi:pudiera}, {cop:saldría} ahora.*
The future seen from the past. Unlike Italian, Spanish uses the simple form: *Dijo que {cop:vendría}.*
A guess about the past: *{cop:Serían} las ocho cuando {pr:llegó}.*

condicional_compuesto.title: Condicional compuesto
body: Use the *condicional simple* of *haber* and the participle.

ul: A result that did not happen: *Si {cst:hubiera estudiado}, {cpa:habría aprobado}.*
Unfulfilled intentions: *{cpa:Habría venido}, pero {im:estaba} enfermo.*
Regret: *{cpa:Habría preferido} quedarme en casa.*
A guess about an earlier past: *{cpa:Habrían salido} ya.*

body: In the result clause, the *-ra* subjunctive is a common alternative: *Si lo {cst:hubiera sabido}, {cst:hubiera venido}.*

imperativo.title: Imperativo
imperativo.summary: Commands, requests, advice and instructions, for every way of addressing someone.

head: Form
Used for
rows: Several people you know well, in Spain
Several people, politely; in Latin America it is the only plural

body: The *tú* form looks like the third person of the present. *Vosotros* replaces the final *-r* of the infinitive with *-d*. *Usted, ustedes* and *nosotros* come from the *subjuntivo presente*, so the vowels swap: *-ar* verbs take *-e*, the others *-a*.
*Ir* has an irregular *nosotros*: *{imv:¡Vamos!}* in the affirmative but *{imv:¡No vayamos!}* in the negative.
Every negative command uses the *subjuntivo presente*, including *tú* and *vosotros*.
In the affirmative the pronoun joins the end of the verb, often adding a written accent. In the negative it goes between *no* and the verb.

Two forms lose a letter. *Nosotros* drops the *-s* before *nos*: *levantemos* becomes *levantémonos*. *Vosotros* drops the *-d* before *os*: *levantad* becomes *levantaos*. The one exception is *irse*: *{imv:¡Idos!}*
Object pronouns follow the same rule. With two pronouns, the indirect one comes first.

ul: *{imv:¡Cómpralo!}* (tú), *{imv:¡Cómprelo!}* (usted), *{imv:¡No lo compres!}* (tú)
Two pronouns: *{imv:¡Dámelo!}*, *{imv:¡No me lo des!}*
Commands: *{imv:Cierra} la puerta.*
Requests, softened with *por favor*: *{imv:Páseme} la sal, por favor.*
Advice: *{imv:Descansa} un poco.*
Invitations: *{imv:Venid} a cenar a casa.*
A question is often more polite: *¿{cop:Podrías} cerrar la puerta?*

subjuntivo.title: Subjuntivo
subjuntivo.summary: The mood of what is wished, doubted, felt or not yet real.
body: The subjunctive presents something as subjective, unreal or not yet happened. It mostly appears in clauses introduced by *que* or after certain conjunctions.

ul: Wishes and requests: *Quiero que {csp:vengas}.*
Emotions: *Me alegra que {csp:estés} aquí.*
Doubt and denied opinions: *Dudo que {csp:sea} verdad. No creo que {csp:venga}.*
Impersonal expressions: *Es importante que {csp:lo sepan}.*
Future time after *cuando, en cuanto, hasta que, antes de que*: *Cuando {csp:llegues}, llámame.*
After *para que, aunque* (with an unknown fact), *sin que, a menos que, con tal de que*.
After *ojalá* and often *quizás, tal vez*: *Ojalá {csp:llueva}.*
Relative clauses about something unknown: *Busco a alguien que {csp:hable} ruso.*
Hypotheses with *si*: *Si {csi:pudiera}, {cop:iría}.*

body: Positive opinions take the indicative: *Creo que {ip:es} verdad.*

subjuntivo_presente.title: Subjuntivo presente
subjuntivo_presente.summary: Wishes, doubts and things not yet real, about now or the future.
body: *-ar* verbs take *-e*, the others take *-a*.
Most irregular verbs start from the *yo* form of the present: *tengo: tenga; hago: haga; pongo: ponga; salgo: salga; vengo: venga; digo: diga; conozco: conozca.*
Spelling: *buscar: busque; llegar: llegue; empezar: empiece.* *-ir* stem-changing verbs also change in *nosotros* and *vosotros*: *pedir: pidamos; dormir: durmamos.*
Also: *haber: haya; dar: dé.*

ul: *Espero que {csp:estés} bien.*
*Cuando {csp:termine}, te llamo.*
*Te lo explico para que lo {csp:entiendas}.*
*Ojalá {csp:haga} sol mañana.*

subjuntivo_perfecto.title: Pretérito perfecto de subjuntivo
subjuntivo_perfecto.summary: Thoughts and feelings now about something that has already happened.
body: Use the *subjuntivo presente* of *haber* and the participle.

ul: An earlier action seen from now: *No creo que {csa:haya llegado}.*
Feelings about what has happened: *Me alegra que {csa:hayas venido}.*
An action finished by a future moment: *Cuando {csa:hayas terminado}, avísame.*

subjuntivo_imperfecto.title: Imperfecto de subjuntivo
subjuntivo_imperfecto.summary: The subjunctive after a past verb, in hypotheses and polite requests.
body: Take the third person plural of the *indefinido*, remove *-ron* and add one of two sets of endings. The two are interchangeable in most contexts, and the *-ra* set is more common.
Every irregularity comes from the *indefinido*: *tuvieron: tuviera; fueron: fuera; hicieron: hiciera; dijeron: dijera; pidieron: pidiera.*

ul: After a main verb in the past: *Quería que {csi:vinieras}.*
After a conditional: *Me gustaría que {csi:fuera} verdad.*
Unlikely or unreal hypotheses: *Si {csi:tuviera} dinero, {cop:viajaría}.*
After *como si*: *Habla como si lo {csi:supiera} todo.*
Polite forms of *querer*: *{csi:Quisiera} un café.*

subjuntivo_pluscuamperfecto.title: Pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo
subjuntivo_pluscuamperfecto.summary: The earlier past in the subjunctive, and hypotheses that can no longer come true.
body: Use the *imperfecto de subjuntivo* of *haber* and the participle. Both sets of endings are possible.

ul: An action before a past main verb: *No creía que {cst:hubiera salido}.*
Past hypotheses that did not come true: *Si {cst:hubiera sabido}, {cpa:habría venido}.*
Regrets: *¡Ojalá te {cst:hubiera escuchado}!*
After *como si*: *Me mira como si no me {cst:hubiera visto} nunca.*
